- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above recent peak unless sentiment shifts to negative.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias in 30-day horizon — if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, adjust downward by 1–3%.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” values (no sentiment), model often fails to adjust for market uncertainty; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast to account for hidden volatility.
